- name: Checkout repository from local mirror
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          MIRROR="$HOME/actions-runner-yoloit/mirror/flutter_agent_harness.git"
          cd /tmp
          rm -rf "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE"
          mkdir -p "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE"
          git clone --reference "$MIRROR" --depth=1 \
            https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness.git "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE"
          echo "Checked out: $(git -C $GITHUB_WORKSPACE log -1 --oneline)"

      # Persistent pinned SDK (issue #354): subosito/flutter-action with
      # cache: true on this PERSISTENT runner cost 5m39s setup (untar ~1GB
      # archive) + 8m47s POST (re-tar the whole SDK) per job — 14.5 of
      # 19.7 min around a 4-min build (run 34815041052). The composite
      # action keeps the SDK at ~/actions-runner-yoloit/flutter-sdk with a
      # .fah-version marker: subsecond reuse when the pin is unchanged,
      # exactly one download per pin bump, no cache POST step at all.
      # Still a pinned 3.47.x install — the runner's hardcoded
      # $HOME/.local/flutter is a stale 3.44.4, below the repo floor
      # >=3.47.0 (daily-publish #260).
      - name: Setup Flutter (self-hosted)
        uses: ./.github/actions/setup-flutter-selfhosted
        with:
          flutter-version: '3.47.x'

      - name: Setup environment (self-hosted)
        run: |
          echo "/opt/homebrew/opt/ruby/bin" >> $GITHUB_PATH
          echo "/opt/homebrew/bin" >> $GITHUB_PATH

      # gh-1275 AC3: fail fast before any build minute is spent — the full
      # gate rationale lives in .github/actions/assert-builtin-skills.
      - uses: ./.github/actions/assert-builtin-skills

      # gh-798 AC1/AC2: fail FAST before any build minute is spent when the
      # version about to be stamped is not above ASC's approved floor
      # (#785's class: altool 90062 at the END of the build). Reads the
      # SAME version source the build lane stamps (BUILD_NAME of the
      # version job); the lane skips named without ASC secrets (the upload
      # leg skips too) and fails closed if ASC is unreachable (E1, one
      # retry). The AC4 marker line lands in the leg log either way.
      - name: Assert TestFlight version floor
        working-directory: flutter_app
        env:
          BUILD_NAME: ${{ needs.version.outputs.version }}
          APP_STORE_CONNECT_KEY_ID: ${{ secrets.APP_STORE_CONNECT_KEY_ID }}
          APP_STORE_CONNECT_ISSUER_ID: ${{ secrets.APP_STORE_CONNECT_ISSUER_ID }}
          APP_STORE_CONNECT_KEY_CONTENT: ${{ secrets.APP_STORE_CONNECT_KEY_CONTENT }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          bundle install
          bundle exec fastlane ios assert_version_floor

      # Issue #726 (run 35491603044): pub has no retry for its git-dep
      # mirror clones — one flaky TCP connect to github.com:443 ("Failed
      # to connect ... after 11155 ms") failed the whole leg with no
      # retry. The bounded retry + deterministic-skew fail-fast now lives
      # in the shared composite action every enforce-lockfile pub get in
      # the repo rides (gh-1310; pinned by test/ci_pub_get_retry_guard_
      # test.dart).
      - name: Install Flutter dependencies
        uses: ./.github/actions/flutter-pub-get

      # #1331 size diet: js_widget_runtime declares `test/assets/` as a
      # package asset DIRECTORY, so its 5.6 MB coach_anny.glb test fixture
      # rides every app bundle. Nothing in the app references it (the #1227
      # mac pass verified by grep over flutter_app/lib, packages, lib and
      # the bundled JS apps — only the package's own tests load it, and
      # those live in the package repo). Removing the file is safe: the
      # pubspec declares the directory, not individual files.
      - name: Prune never-loaded package test fixture (#1331)
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          JS_WR=$(python3 -c '
            import json, pathlib
            cfg = json.loads(pathlib.Path("flutter_app/.dart_tool/package_config.json").read_text())
            print(next(p["rootUri"] for p in cfg["packages"] if p["name"] == "js_widget_runtime"))
          ')
          case "$JS_WR" in
            file://*) JS_WR=${JS_WR#file://} ;;
          esac
          case "$JS_WR" in
            /*) ;;
            *) JS_WR="$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/$JS_WR" ;;
          esac
          GLB="$JS_WR/test/assets/coach_anny.glb"
          if [ -f "$GLB" ]; then
            rm -f "$GLB"
            echo "pruned coach_anny.glb (5.6 MB never-loaded test fixture, #1331) from $JS_WR"
          else
            echo "coach_anny.glb already absent — nothing to prune"
          fi

      # The workspace is re-cloned every run, which wipes Pods/ and forces a
      # full pod install. Cache it keyed by the lockfile; $HOME-level caches
      # (pub-cache, CocoaPods download cache, Ruby gems, Flutter SDK) already
      # persist on the self-hosted runner.
      # v2: bust the cache — the Podfile.lock was stale (cupertino_http added
      # in 4bcac41 but the lockfile wasn't regenerated), so cached Pods were
      # missing the plugin's native code entirely. The build step's
      # `flutter build ios` runs `pod install` which regenerates the lockfile
      # with all registered plugins.
      - name: Cache CocoaPods (iOS)
        uses: actions/cache@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9 # v6.1.0
        with:
          path: flutter_app/ios/Pods
          key: ios-pods-v2-${{ hashFiles('flutter_app/ios/Podfile.lock') }}

      - name: Restore vendored WasmRun iOS framework
        timeout-minutes: 15
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          # The prebuilt XCFramework is excluded from git. Prefer the local
          # working copy on this self-hosted runner; fall back to the upstream
          # release asset if the local copy is unavailable.
          LOCAL_SRC="/Users/Uladzimir_Klyshevich/git/flutter_agent/vendor/wasm_run_flutter/ios/Frameworks/WasmRun.xcframework"
          DEST="vendor/wasm_run_flutter/ios/Frameworks"
          rm -rf "$DEST/WasmRun.xcframework"
          mkdir -p "$DEST"
          if [ -d "$LOCAL_SRC" ]; then
            echo "Using local framework: $LOCAL_SRC"
            cp -R "$LOCAL_SRC" "$DEST/"
          else
            echo "Local framework not found, downloading from upstream release..."
            # --retry alone skips transient mid-transfer resets (curl 56) —
            # the run-34709113737 failure: reset 3s into the 92.7 MB asset.
            curl -L --retry 3 --retry-all-errors --retry-delay 10 --max-time 600 \
              -o /tmp/WasmRun.xcframework.zip \
              https://github.com/juancastillo0/wasm_run/releases/download/wasm_run-v0.1.0/WasmRun.xcframework.zip
            unzip -q /tmp/WasmRun.xcframework.zip -d "$DEST"
          fi
          ls -la "$DEST/WasmRun.xcframework"

      - name: Validate iOS secrets
        env:
          IOS_P12_BASE64: ${{ secrets.IOS_P12_BASE64 }}
          IOS_P12_PASSWORD: ${{ secrets.IOS_P12_PASSWORD }}
          IOS_PROVISIONING_PROFILE_BASE64: ${{ secrets.IOS_PROVISIONING_PROFILE_BASE64 }}
        run: |
          if [ -z "$IOS_P12_BASE64" ]; then
            echo "::error::IOS_P12_BASE64 secret is not set"
            exit 1
          fi
          if [ -z "$IOS_P12_PASSWORD" ]; then
            echo "::error::IOS_P12_PASSWORD secret is not set"
            exit 1
          fi
          if [ -z "$IOS_PROVISIONING_PROFILE_BASE64" ]; then
            echo "::error::IOS_PROVISIONING_PROFILE_BASE64 secret is not set"
            exit 1
          fi
          echo "All required iOS secrets are present"

      - name: Import certificates and provisioning profile
        env:
          IOS_P12_BASE64: ${{ secrets.IOS_P12_BASE64 }}
          IOS_P12_PASSWORD: ${{ secrets.IOS_P12_PASSWORD }}
          IOS_PROVISIONING_PROFILE_BASE64: ${{ secrets.IOS_PROVISIONING_PROFILE_BASE64 }}
          IOS_LIVE_ACTIVITY_PROFILE_BASE64: ${{ secrets.IOS_LIVE_ACTIVITY_PROFILE_BASE64 }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          # Create a temporary keychain for this run (same pattern as learn.ai).
          security delete-keychain build.keychain 2>/dev/null || true
          secur…

# create profiles). Its App Store profile rides its own secret.

            exit 1

      - name: Ensure iOS device SDK is available
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          echo "Available iOS SDKs:"
          xcodebuild -showsdks | grep iphoneos || true
          echo "Downloading iOS platform if missing..."
          xcodebuild -downloadPlatform iOS || true
          # The attached device may run a newer iOS than the installed SDK;
          # try to download the matching version. If this fails, the build
          # will still fail with a clearer message.
          xcodebuild -downloadPlatform iOS -buildVersion 26.5 || true

      - name: Create placeholder .env asset
        working-directory: flutter_app
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          cat > .env << 'EOF'
          OPENROUTER_API_KEY=
          MODEL_ID=
          BASE_URL=
          HUGGINGFACE_TOKEN=
          EOF

      # The plist is gitignored, so the fresh CI checkout has none and the
      # native Firebase SDK logs I-COR000012/0008 at startup. Inject it from
      # a secret when available (same dev.fa1.app registration as
      # firebase_options.dart).
      - name: Write GoogleService-Info.plist (iOS)
        env:
          GOOGLE_SERVICE_INFO_PLIST_BASE64: ${{ secrets.GOOGLE_SERVICE_INFO_PLIST_BASE64 }}
        run: |
          if [ -n "$GOOGLE_SERVICE_INFO_PLIST_BASE64" ]; then
            echo "$GOOGLE_SERVICE_INFO_PLIST_BASE64" | base64 --decode > flutter_app/ios/Runner/GoogleService-Info.plist
            echo "GoogleService-Info.plist written (bundle: $(plutil -extract BUNDLE_ID raw flutter_app/ios/Runner/GoogleService-Info.plist))"
          else
            echo "⚠️ GOOGLE_SERVICE_INFO_PLIST_BASE64 not set — building without the native Firebase plist"
          fi

      - name: Build iOS IPA
        working-directory: flutter_app
        env:
          BUILD_NUMBER: ${{ github.run_number }}
          # Issue #726 (run 35564638018): ASC closed the 1.0.0 train once a
          # 1.0.0 build was approved (error 90186) and rejects new builds
          # whose CFBundleShortVersionString is not higher than the
          # previously approved version (error 90062) — pubspec pins 1.0.0,
          # so the daily train stalled forever. Ship the derived next-tag
          # version (e.g. 0.1.446), which strictly increases.
          BUILD_NAME: ${{ needs.version.outputs.version }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          export PATH="/opt/homebrew/opt/ruby/bin:/opt/homebrew/bin:$PATH"
          bundle install

          PROFILE=~/Library/MobileDevice/Provisioning\ Profiles/profile.mobileprovision
          UUID=$(security cms -D -i "$PROFILE" 2>/dev/null | plutil -extract UUID raw -)
          TEAM_ID=$(security cms -D -i "$PROFILE" 2>/dev/null | plutil -extract TeamIdentifier.0 raw -)
          BUNDLE_ID=$(security cms -D -i "$PROFILE" 2>/dev/null | plutil -extract Entitlements.application-identifier raw - | sed "s/^$TEAM_ID.//")
          PROFILE_NAME=$(security cms -D -i "$PROFILE" 2>/dev/null | plutil -extract Name raw -)
          echo "PROFILE_NAME=$PROFILE_NAME"

          LA_PROFILE=~/Library/MobileDevice/Provisioning\ Profiles/liveactivity.mobileprovision
          LA_PROFILE_NAME=$(security cms -D -i "$LA_PROFILE" 2>/dev/null | plutil -extract Name raw -)
          echo "LA_PROFILE_NAME=$LA_PROFILE_NAME"

          IOS_TEAM_ID="$TEAM_ID" \
          IOS_BUNDLE_ID="$BUNDLE_ID" \
          IOS_PROVISIONING_PROFILE_NAME="$PROFILE_NAME" \
          IOS_LIVE_ACTIVITY_PROFILE_NAME="$LA_PROFILE_NAME" \
          IOS_SIGNING_IDENTITY="iPhone Distribution" \
          bundle exec fastlane ios build_only

      # #1331 size diet: the exported IPA ships ~99 MB (uncompressed) of
      # debug dSYMs under Symbols/. App Store Connect strips that directory
      # from device delivery anyway (TestFlight reports ~157 MB — the
      # payload WITHOUT Symbols), so it is dead weight in the artifact.
      # Repack without it: Payload/ is untouched (codesign validity lives
      # inside the bundle), zip -y preserves the framework symlinks so the
      # manifest shape is unchanged. Idempotent — a future export that
      # omits Symbols/ skips straight through.
      - name: Strip debug symbols from IPA (#1331)
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          IPA_PATH=$(find flutter_app/build/ios -name "*.ipa" -type f | head -1)
          if [ -z "$IPA_PATH" ]; then
            echo "::error::IPA file not found in flutter_app/build/ios"
            exit 1
          fi
          if ! unzip -l "$IPA_PATH" "Symbols/*" | grep -q "Symbols/"; then
            echo "no Symbols/ in the IPA — nothing to strip"
            exit 0
          fi
          STRIP=$(mktemp -d)
          unzip -q "$IPA_PATH" -d "$STRIP"
          rm -rf "$STRIP/Symbols"
          BEFORE=$(stat -f%z "$IPA_PATH")
          rm -f "$IPA_PATH"
          (cd "$STRIP" && find . -mindepth 1 -maxdepth 1 -exec zip -qyr9 "$IPA_PATH" {} +)
          rm -rf "$STRIP"
          AFTER=$(stat -f%z "$IPA_PATH")
          echo "IPA stripped: $BEFORE -> $AFTER bytes ($((BEFORE - AFTER)) saved compressed)"

      - name: Upload IPA Artifact
        # Uploaded before the symbol gate so a failed gate still leaves the
        # IPA available for debugging.
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@043fb46d1a93c77aae656e7c1c64a875d1fc6a0a # v7.0.1
        with:
          name: ios-ipa
          path: flutter_app/build/ios/ipa/*.ipa
          retention-days: 14

      # #1331 ratchet: per-file uncompressed floor seeded from the last
      # release-shape CI artifact (run 37495702186 fa.ipa) with the diet
      # applied. Growth >5% on any line or TOTAL, or a re-added heavy line
      # (e.g. Symbols/ or coach_anny.glb coming back), fails the leg —
      # same gate family as the macOS pass (#1227). Also pins the owner
      # hard constraint: the js-apps WASM runtime and LiteRT LM always ship.
      - name: Size manifest ratchet + wasm keep-set (#1331)
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          IPA_PATH=$(find flutter_app/build/ios -name "*.ipa" -type f | head -1)
          MANIFEST=$(mktemp)
          python3 scripts/size_manifest.py check "$IPA_PATH" \
            --baseline scripts/size_budget/fa-ios.tsv --manifest-out "$MANIFEST"
          for ASSET in \
            flutter_assets/assets/wasm/python.wasm \
            flutter_assets/assets/wasm/qjs.wasm \
            flutter_assets/assets/wasm/coreutils.wasm \
            flutter_assets/assets/wasm/lua.wasm; do
            grep -q "$ASSET" "$MANIFEST" || {
              echo "::error::$ASSET missing from the IPA — the js-apps WASM runtime must always ship (owner directive, #1331)"
              exit 1

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Per-artifact uncompressed size manifest + budget gate (#1096 AC1).

Emits the per-entry uncompressed size table (the issue's inventory format)
for a shipped artifact and fails the build when any tracked line regresses
beyond the budget (default +5%).

Usage:
  size_manifest.py emit   <artifact> [--min-bytes N]        # TSV to stdout
  size_manifest.py check  <artifact> --baseline FILE
                          [--budget-pct 5] [--init-if-missing]
                          [--manifest-out FILE]
  size_manifest.py selftest

`<artifact>` is a zip-family file (.zip/.ipa/.aab — uncompressed entry sizes
via zipfile) or a directory (tree of file sizes, for the web deploy root).

Manifest format (TSV; every row is `<bytes>\t<name>`, path-sorted. TOTAL
is an ordinary row — `<total_bytes>\tTOTAL` — and sorts among the paths;
do not rely on its position, the parser keys by name):
  <uncompressed_bytes>\t<path>
  <total_bytes>\tTOTAL

Gate semantics (`check`):
  - growth > budget%% on any baseline line or on TOTAL  -> FAIL
  - NEW line heavier than 5%% of the baseline TOTAL     -> FAIL
    (catches re-adding removed weight, e.g. a dropped interpreter coming
    back; canvaskit rev-dir churn on Flutter upgrades trips this too —
    that is by design: re-growth must be a conscious ack)
  - removed lines are improvements, reported only
  - --init-if-missing: no baseline file yet -> write it and pass with a
    loud notice (ratchet bootstrap; commit the file to arm the gate)
  - --reseed: overwrite an EXISTING baseline from this artifact and pass
    with a notice — the escape hatch for intentional growth; commit the
    rewritten file to make the new shape the floor

CI escape hatch for intentional growth: re-run locally with the same
artifact and `--reseed`, commit the rewritten baseline.
"""

import argparse
import sys
import zipfile
from pathlib import Path

# Per-line tracking floor: smaller files are noise (thousands of them
# jitter by whole percentages); the TOTAL line covers their aggregate.
MIN_BYTES = 64 * 1024
# A brand-new tracked line heavier than this share of the old TOTAL is
# re-growth, not rounding — fail it.
NEW_LINE_SHARE = 0.05


def iter_sizes(artifact: Path):
    """Yield (path, uncompressed_bytes) for every file in the artifact."""
    if artifact.is_file():
        # zip-family: .zip / .ipa / .aab / .apk
        with zipfile.ZipFile(artifact) as zf:
            for info in zf.infolist():
                if info.is_dir():
                    continue
                yield info.filename.replace("\t", " "), info.file_size
        return
    if artifact.is_dir():
        for p in sorted(artifact.rglob("*")):
            if p.is_file() and not p.is_symlink():
                yield p.relative_to(artifact).as_posix().replace("\t", " "), p.stat().st_size
        return
    raise SystemExit(f"size_manifest: artifact not found: {artifact}")


def build_manifest(artifact: Path, min_bytes: int) -> "dict[str, int]":
    sizes = dict(iter_sizes(artifact))
    manifest = {p: n for p, n in sizes.items() if n >= min_bytes}
    manifest["TOTAL"] = sum(sizes.values())
    return manifest


def fmt_table(manifest: "dict[str, int]") -> str:
    width = max((len(p) for p in manifest), default=5)
    lines = [f"{manifest[p]:>12}  {p.ljust(width)}" for p in sorted(manifest) if p != "TOTAL"]
    lines.append("-" * (width + 14))
    lines.append(f"{manifest['TOTAL']:>12}  TOTAL")
    return "\n".join(lines)


def load_baseline(path: Path) -> "dict[str, int]":
    baseline = {}
    for line in path.read_text().splitlines():
        if not line.strip():
            continue
        size, _, name = line.partition("\t")
        baseline[name] = int(size)
    if "TOTAL" not in baseline:
        raise SystemExit(f"size_manifest: baseline {path} has no TOTAL line")
    return baseline


def write_baseline(path: Path, manifest: "dict[str, int]") -> None:
    path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    lines = [f"{manifest[p]}\t{p}" for p in sorted(manifest)]
    path.write_text("\n".join(lines) + "\n")


def check(artifact: Path, baseline_path: Path, budget_pct: float,
          init_if_missing: bool = False, reseed: bool = False,
          manifest_out=None) -> int:
    manifest = build_manifest(artifact, MIN_BYTES)
    if manifest_out:
        write_baseline(manifest_out, manifest)

    if not baseline_path.exists():
        if init_if_missing:
            write_baseline(baseline_path, manifest)
            print(f"::notice::size_manifest: baseline initialized from this "
                  f"artifact — COMMIT {baseline_path} to arm the gate")
            print(fmt_table(manifest))
            return 0
        print(f"::error::size_manifest: baseline {baseline_path} missing "
              f"(run with --init-if-missing to seed it)")
        return 2

    if reseed:
        write_baseline(baseline_path, manifest)
        print(f"::notice::size_manifest: baseline RESEEDED from this "
              f"artifact — {baseline_path} rewritten; COMMIT it to make "
              f"the new shape the floor")
        print(fmt_table(manifest))
        return 0

    baseline = load_baseline(baseline_path)
    base_total = baseline["TOTAL"]
    failures = []
    grew, shrank, new, removed = [], [], [], []

    for name in sorted(set(baseline) | set(manifest)):
        if name == "TOTAL":
            continue
        old, cur = baseline.get(name), manifest.get(name)
        if old is None and cur is not None:
            new.append((name, cur))
        elif cur is None:
            removed.append((name, old))
        elif cur > old:
            grew.append((name, old, cur))
        elif cur < old:
            shrank.append((name, old, cur))

    for name, old, cur in grew:
        pct = (cur - old) / old * 100 if old else float("inf")
        if pct > budget_pct:
            failures.append(f"  GREW    +{pct:6.1f}%  {name}  {old} -> {cur}")
    total_pct = (manifest["TOTAL"] - base_total) / base_total * 100 if base_total else 0.0
    if total_pct > budget_pct:
        failures.append(f"  TOTAL   +{total_pct:6.1f}%  {base_total} -> {manifest['TOTAL']}")
    for name, cur in new:
        if cur > NEW_LINE_SHARE * base_total:
            failures.append(f"  NEW     {'':>8}  {name}  {cur} bytes "
                            f"(> {NEW_LINE_SHARE:.0%} of baseline TOTAL)")

          f"baseline: {baseline_path})")
    print(fmt_table(manifest))
    if shrank:
        print(f"improvements: {len(shrank)} line(s) shrank, "
              f"{len(removed)} line(s) removed")
        for name, old, cur in shrank[:10]:
            print(f"  shrank  {name}  {old} -> {cur}")
        for name, old in removed[:10]:
            print(f"  removed {name}  ({old} bytes)")
    if failures:
        print(f"::error::size budget regression in {artifact} "
              f"({len(failures)} line(s) beyond +{budget_pct}%):")
        for f in failures:
            print(f)
        print("intentional growth? re-seed the floor with: python3 "
              "scripts/size_manifest.py check <artifact> --baseline "
              f"{baseline_path} --reseed")
        return 1
    print(f"size budget OK (TOTAL {total_pct:+.1f}% vs baseline)")
    return 0

Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Impact analysis (CodeGraph or grep fallback) Use CodeGraph to find "what could break": - `codegraph_callers` / `codegraph_callees` on modified public symbols - `codegraph_search` for: `PAT_TOKEN`, `secrets.`, `github.token`, `previousViewModel` - `codegraph_impact` before flagging architectural changes **If CodeGraph unavailable**, use grep and document it: ```bash grep -rn "changedFunctionName" --include="*.ts" . grep -rn "secrets\.\|github\.token" . ``` ## 5. Review dimensions Rate the PR across all relevant dimensions: | Dimension | What to check | |---|---| | **Security** | injection, unsafe interpolation, secret leakage, missing permissions, unsafe defaults | | **Architecture / OOP** | SRP, coupling, abstraction consistency, provider/repository boundaries | | **Code quality** | naming, complexity, error handling, logging, comments | | **Tests** | coverage for new/changed paths, meaningful assertions, no brittle string-only tests | | **Duplication** | copy-paste, duplicated logic across files, duplicated configuration | | **Backward compatibility** | public API changes, migration paths, default behavior | | **Performance** | unnecessary rebuilds, heavy sync operations, missing timeouts | | **Workflow / CI safety** | (when `.github/workflows/` changes) secret declarations, ref pinning, permissions, timeouts | ## 6. Severity classification Classify every finding before writing outputs: - **BLOCKING** — merge would cause a bug, security issue, data loss, or CI break. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. blocks.text:
# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (`scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh` stage_size + ci.yml guard, both covering
  `lib test example bin flutter_app/lib`). Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
  (never replaces), so injected vars keep the inherited environment.
- `lib/src/env/io_execution_env.dart` — `LocalShell`: foreground `exec`
  runs under `setsid` when the host has it (probe
  `ownProcessGroupAvailable`, seam `ownProcessGroupOverride`) and the
  timeout/cancel paths reap the whole tree (`killTree` + direct-kill
  backstop) with a capped pipe-drain (`_drainGrace`) — timeout/cancel'd
  calls complete in ≤ timeout + kill grace + drain grace; a no-timeout
  call within `_drainGrace` of the direct child's exit (the drain is
  capped unconditionally: after the child is reaped every remaining pipe

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1333
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1333
- **Title**: feat(1331): iOS size diet — IPA dSYM strip + never-loaded fixture prune + ratchet
- **Author**: vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit
- **Branch**: `feat/1331-ios-size-diet` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 2
- **Additions**: +127
- **Deletions**: -0
- **Created**: 2026-10-06T19:18:32Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-06T19:18:32Z

## PR Description

Closes #1331

## Size evidence (CI-only, per repo rule)

Source: **run 37495702186** (`build-mobile (none/all)`, head `af1064b04605`, created 2026-10-06T16:26Z) → `Build iOS IPA` job 112380365429; job log line `IPA built successfully: … 84310520 … flutter_app/build/ios/ipa/fa.ipa` (fastlane `build_app`, `export_method: "app-store"` — `flutter_app/fastlane/Fastfile:427-432`). Downloaded the `ios-ipa` artifact (id 11429033818) and ran the repo's own tool on it: `python3 scripts/size_manifest.py emit fa.ipa` → per-file manifest, TOTAL **253,948,172 B uncompressed**, 84,310,520 B compressed. The downloaded artifact byte-size-matches the CI log line exactly (84,310,520). No local iOS build was used for any number (fleet Mac has no signing/toolchain; local iOS AOT sizes are known to lie — hence CI-log-only).

## Manifest — classification of every heavy artifact (uncompressed)

| Artifact | Bytes | Verdict |
|---|---|---|
| `Symbols/*` — 8 dSYM files (4C4C4498… 57.9 MB, 0CDEA45A… 16.9 MB, 27399001… 11.2 MB, 7CFA843F… 9.9 MB, 1F0AF668… 2.6 MB, +3 small) | **98,989,120** | **EVICT** — debug dSYMs in a release IPA |
| `flutter_assets/assets/wasm/*` — 13 entries (python.wasm 30.4 MB, coreutils 8.4 MB, lua 4.7 MB, python_stdlib.zip 2.9 MB, rg 2.8 MB, sed 2.3 MB, awk 2.2 MB, find 1.7 MB, sqlite3 1.7 MB, qjs 1.5 MB, zip 0.4 MB, gzip/tar ~0.3 MB) | 59,362,102 | **KEEP** — owner hard constraint: the js-apps WASM runtime stays (mobile `WasiSandboxShell` loads these via rootBundle; the #1227 mac cut was desktop-only for exactly this reason) |
| `App.framework/App` (Dart AOT) | 28,336,528 | KEEP — the app |
| `LiteRtLm.framework` | 17,025,248 | **KEEP** — owner hard constraint (on-device LLM) |
| `GemmaModelConstraintProvider.framework` | 11,866,224 | **KEEP** — owner hard constraint (on-device stack) |
| `Runner` | 10,877,488 | KEEP — app binary (wasm_run force_load + cupertino_http trampolines, CI-verified per build) |
| `Flutter.framework` + `icudtl.dat` | 10,281,184 | KEEP — engine, pinned (#1096 non-goal) |
| `LiteRtMetalAccelerator.framework` | 5,466,480 | **KEEP** — owner hard constraint (on-device stack) |
| `js_widget_runtime/test/assets/coach_anny.glb` | **5,621,868** | **EVICT** — never-loaded test fixture |
| `sqlite3.framework` | 1,648,704 | KEEP |
| Fonts (Inter ×4, JetBrainsMono ×2, CupertinoIcons) | 2,471,060 | KEEP — all loaded by the UI; **no duplicate fonts found** in the IPA manifest (each file appears exactly once) |
| FaLiveActivity.appex / StreamProxy / objective_c / libswiftCompatibilitySpan ×2 / Assets.car | ~851,000 | KEEP — platform plumbing / Live Activity feature |
| `flutter_inappwebview` t_rex.html + web_support.js | 171,568 | KEEP — 0.17 MB; evicting package demo assets would need pre-build package surgery below the cost/benefit line (noted, deliberately skipped) |
| NOTICES.Z | 126,278 | KEEP — legal |

## Evictions + why

1. **`Symbols/` (98,989,120 B uncompressed, 8 dSYM files).** App Store Connect strips this directory from device delivery anyway — TestFlight's ~157 MB report for 1.0.519 matches the payload *without* Symbols (payload 253,948,172 − Symbols 98,989,120 − SwiftSupport 171,952 ≈ 154.8 MB). So inside the shipped IPA it is pure dead weight; only crash-symbolication upload to ASC loses dSYMs (disclosed trade, in-scope per the issue's "symbols" target). Cut: repack the IPA without `Symbols/` after the fastlane export (`build-mobile.yml` "Strip debug symbols from IPA"); `Payload/` is untouched so the codesign stays valid, `zip -y` preserves framework symlinks so the manifest shape is byte-identical. Idempotent: a future export without Symbols/ skips through.
2. **`coach_anny.glb` (5,621,868 B).** js_widget_runtime declares `test/assets/` as a package asset *directory* (upstream pubspec), so the fixture rides every bundle; nothing in the app references it (verified by the #1227 mac pass over flutter_app/lib, packages, lib, bundled JS apps — only the package's own tests load it, and those live in the package repo, not here). Cut: delete the file from the materialized package pre-build ("Prune never-loaded package test fixture" step, resolves the path from `.dart_tool/package_config.json`); directory-declared assets tolerate the missing file. Self-healing if pub re-clones the dep.

Not done: `upload_symbols: false` via ExportOptions — Xcode's Symbols/-in-IPA behavior is not verifiable without a real signed build here; the strip step is deterministic either way.

## Expected IPA delta (from CI numbers)

| Measure | Before (CI) | After | Δ |
|---|---|---|---|
| IPA uncompressed TOTAL | 253,948,172 | 149,337,184 | **−104,610,988 (−41.2%)** |
| IPA compressed (release asset) | 84,310,520 | **59,281,742 (measured on the repacked CI artifact)** | **−25,028,778 (−29.7%)** |
| TestFlight device size | ~157 MB | ~151 MB | −5.6 MB (the glb; Symbols never reached devices — ASC strips them) |

## Ratchet

`scripts/size_budget/fa-ios.tsv` (38 lines + TOTAL) seeded from the CI artifact with the diet applied — the exact post-cut floor. Wired into the build-ios leg: `python3 scripts/size_manifest.py check <ipa> --baseline scripts/size_budget/fa-ios.tsv` (+5% per-line and TOTAL budget, NEW-line guard) — same tool and semantics as the mac pass (#1227). The same step pins the owner hard constraint: the leg fails if `assets/wasm/{python,qjs,coreutils,lua}.wasm` or `LiteRtLm.framework` ever leave the IPA.

## Gate proofs (all local, against the CI artifact — no local iOS build)

- `size_manifest.py selftest` → **PASS**
- Failing-first: uncut CI IPA vs new floor → **exit 1**, `TOTAL +70.1%`, `Symbols/*` heavy lines flagged `NEW` — the ratchet demonstrably bites on the pre-diet shape
- Post-cut shape (repack of the CI IPA: `Symbols/` stripped, glb removed) vs floor → **exit 0**, `TOTAL -0.0%` (every entry byte-identical to the floor — symlink-preserving rezip changes no sizes)
- Keep-set assertions on the cut manifest: python/qjs/coreutils/lua wasm + LiteRtLm all present, `coach_anny` absent
- Workflow YAML re-parsed; build-ios step order: pub get → prune → build → strip → upload → ratchet+keep-set → FFI verify

## Honest disclosure

- No local iOS build exists in this PR: the fleet Mac cannot sign or build iOS, and per fleet policy local iOS AOT sizes are not evidence anyway. Every number above comes from CI run 37495702186's artifact + job log. The "post-cut" shape was produced by locally repacking **that CI artifact** with the exact commands the new strip step runs (plus the glb deletion the build-time prune does); the first CI-ios leg on this PR's merge train is the real end-to-end proof (device acceptance likewise CI/post-merge — js-apps wasm smoke is enforced statically by the keep-set gate here).
- Android legs, LiteRT, the WASM runtime, and the FFI-verify step are untouched.
- Fleet policy: this PR does not dispatch or rerun workflows; SM schedules CI.

index 1e83a3937..69f423c73 100644
--- a/.github/workflows/build-mobile.yml
+++ b/.github/workflows/build-mobile.yml
@@ -662,6 +662,36 @@ jobs:
       - name: Install Flutter dependencies
         uses: ./.github/actions/flutter-pub-get
 
+      # #1331 size diet: js_widget_runtime declares `test/assets/` as a
+      # package asset DIRECTORY, so its 5.6 MB coach_anny.glb test fixture
+      # rides every app bundle. Nothing in the app references it (the #1227
+      # mac pass verified by grep over flutter_app/lib, packages, lib and
+      # the bundled JS apps — only the package's own tests load it, and
+      # those live in the package repo). Removing the file is safe: the
+      # pubspec declares the directory, not individual files.
+      - name: Prune never-loaded package test fixture (#1331)
+        run: |
+          set -euo pipefail
+          JS_WR=$(python3 -c '
+            import json, pathlib
+            cfg = json.loads(pathlib.Path("flutter_app/.dart_tool/package_config.json").read_text())
+            print(next(p["rootUri"] for p in cfg["packages"] if p["name"] == "js_widget_runtime"))
+          ')
+          case "$JS_WR" in
+            file://*) JS_WR=${JS_WR#file://} ;;
+          esac
+          case "$JS_WR" in
+            /*) ;;
+            *) JS_WR="$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/$JS_WR" ;;
+          esac
+          GLB="$JS_WR/test/assets/coach_anny.glb"
+          if [ -f "$GLB" ]; then
+            rm -f "$GLB"
+            echo "pruned coach_anny.glb (5.6 MB never-loaded test fixture, #1331) from $JS_WR"
+          else
+            echo "coach_anny.glb already absent — nothing to prune"
+          fi
+
       # The workspace is re-cloned every run, which wipes Pods/ and forces a
       # full pod install. Cache it keyed by the lockfile; $HOME-level caches
       # (pub-cache, CocoaPods download cache, Ruby gems, Flutter SDK) already
@@ -827,6 +857,36 @@ jobs:
           IOS_SIGNING_IDENTITY="iPhone Distribution" \
           bundle exec fastlane ios build_only
 
+      # #1331 size diet: the exported IPA ships ~99 MB (uncompressed) of
+      # debug dSYMs under Symbols/. App Store Connect strips that directory
+      # from device delivery anyway (TestFlight reports ~157 MB — the
+      # payload WITHOUT Symbols), so it is dead weight in the artifact.

+      # inside the bundle), zip -y preserves the framework symlinks so the
+      # manifest shape is unchanged. Idempotent — a future export that
+      # omits Symbols/ skips straight through.
+      - name: Strip debug symbols from IPA (#1331)
+        run: |
+          set -euo pipefail
+          IPA_PATH=$(find flutter_app/build/ios -name "*.ipa" -type f | head -1)
+          if [ -z "$IPA_PATH" ]; then
+            echo "::error::IPA file not found in flutter_app/build/ios"
+            exit 1
+          fi
+          if ! unzip -l "$IPA_PATH" "Symbols/*" | grep -q "Symbols/"; then
+            echo "no Symbols/ in the IPA — nothing to strip"
+            exit 0
+          fi
+          STRIP=$(mktemp -d)
+          unzip -q "$IPA_PATH" -d "$STRIP"
+          rm -rf "$STRIP/Symbols"
+          BEFORE=$(stat -f%z "$IPA_PATH")
+          rm -f "$IPA_PATH"
+          (cd "$STRIP" && find . -mindepth 1 -maxdepth 1 -exec zip -qyr9 "$IPA_PATH" {} +)
+          rm -rf "$STRIP"
+          AFTER=$(stat -f%z "$IPA_PATH")
+          echo "IPA stripped: $BEFORE -> $AFTER bytes ($((BEFORE - AFTER)) saved compressed)"
+
       - name: Upload IPA Artifact

         # IPA available for debugging.
@@ -836,6 +896,35 @@ jobs:

+      # release-shape CI artifact (run 37495702186 fa.ipa) with the diet
+      # applied. Growth >5% on any line or TOTAL, or a re-added heavy line
+      # (e.g. Symbols/ or coach_anny.glb coming back), fails the leg —

+      # hard constraint: the js-apps WASM runtime and LiteRT LM always ship.

{
  "key": "pr-1333",
  "fields": {
    "summary": "feat(1331): iOS size diet — IPA dSYM strip + never-loaded fixture prune + ratchet",
    "description": "Closes #1331

## Size evidence (CI-only, per repo rule)

Source: **run 37495702186** (`build-mobile (none/all)`, head `af1064b04605`, created 2026-10-06T16:26Z) → `Build iOS IPA` job 112380365429; job log line `IPA built successfully: … 84310520 … flutter_app/build/ios/ipa/fa.ipa` (fastlane `build_app`, `export_method: "app-store"` — `flutter_app/fastlane/Fastfile:427-432`). Downloaded the `ios-ipa` artifact (id 11429033818) and ran the repo's own tool on it: `python3 scripts/size_manifest.py emit fa.ipa` → per-file manifest, TOTAL **253,948,172 B uncompressed**, 84,310,520 B compressed. The downloaded artifact byte-size-matches the CI log line exactly (84,310,520). No local iOS build was used for any number (fleet Mac has no signing/toolchain; local iOS AOT sizes are known to lie — hence CI-log-only).

## Manifest — classification of every heavy artifact (uncompressed)

| Artifact | Bytes | Verdict |
|---|---|---|
| `Symbols/*` — 8 dSYM files (4C4C4498… 57.9 MB, 0CDEA45A… 16.9 MB, 27399001… 11.2 MB, 7CFA843F… 9.9 MB, 1F0AF668… 2.6 MB, +3 small) | **98,989,120** | **EVICT** — debug dSYMs in a release IPA |
| `flutter_assets/assets/wasm/*` — 13 entries (python.wasm 30.4 MB, coreutils 8.4 MB, lua 4.7 MB, python_stdlib.zip 2.9 MB, rg 2.8 MB, sed 2.3 MB, awk 2.2 MB, find 1.7 MB, sqlite3 1.7 MB, qjs 1.5 MB, zip 0.4 MB, gzip/tar ~0.3 MB) | 59,362,102 | **KEEP** — owner hard constraint: the js-apps WASM runtime stays (mobile `WasiSandboxShell` loads these via rootBundle; the #1227 mac cut was desktop-only for exactly this reason) |
| `App.framework/App` (Dart AOT) | 28,336,528 | KEEP — the app |
| `LiteRtLm.framework` | 17,025,248 | **KEEP** — owner hard constraint (on-device LLM) |
| `GemmaModelConstraintProvider.framework` | 11,866,224 | **KEEP** — owner hard constraint (on-device stack) |
| `Runner` | 10,877,488 | KEEP — app binary (wasm_run force_load + cupertino_http trampolines, CI-verified per build) |
| `Flutter.framework` + `icudtl.dat` | 10,281,184 | KEEP — engine, pinned (#1096 non-goal) |
| `LiteRtMetalAccelerator.framework` | 5,466,480 | **KEEP** — owner hard constraint (on-device stack) |
| `js_widget_runtime/test/assets/coach_anny.glb` | **5,621,868** | **EVICT** — never-loaded test fixture |
| `sqlite3.framework` | 1,648,704 | KEEP |
| Fonts (Inter ×4, JetBrainsMono ×2, CupertinoIcons) | 2,471,060 | KEEP — all loaded by the UI; **no duplicate fonts found** in the IPA manifest (each file appears exactly once) |
| FaLiveActivity.appex / StreamProxy / objective_c / libswiftCompatibilitySpan ×2 / Assets.car | ~851,000 | KEEP — platform plumbing / Live Activity feature |
| `flutter_inappwebview` t_rex.html + web_support.js | 171,568 | KEEP — 0.17 MB; evicting package demo assets would need pre-build package surgery below the cost/benefit line (noted, deliberately skipped) |
| NOTICES.Z | 126,278 | KEEP — legal |

## Evictions + why

1. **`Symbols/` (98,989,120 B uncompressed, 8 dSYM files).** App Store Connect strips this directory from device delivery anyway — TestFlight's ~157 MB report for 1.0.519 matches the payload *without* Symbols (payload 253,948,172 − Symbols 98,989,120 − SwiftSupport 171,952 ≈ 154.8 MB). So inside the shipped IPA it is pure dead weight; only crash-symbolication upload to ASC loses dSYMs (disclosed trade, in-scope per the issue's "symbols" target). Cut: repack the IPA without `Symbols/` after the fastlane export (`build-mobile.yml` "Strip debug symbols from IPA"); `Payload/` is untouched so the codesign stays valid, `zip -y` preserves framework symlinks so the manifest shape is byte-identical. Idempotent: a future export without Symbols/ skips through.
2. **`coach_anny.glb` (5,621,868 B).** js_widget_runtime declares `test/assets/` as a package asset *directory* (upstream pubspec), so the fixture rides every bundle; nothing in the app references it (verified by the #1227 mac pass over flutter_app/lib, packages, lib, bundled JS apps — only the package's own tests load it, and those live in the package repo, not here). Cut: delete the file from the materialized package pre-build ("Prune never-loaded package test fixture" step, resolves the path from `.dart_tool/package_config.json`); directory-declared assets tolerate the missing file. Self-healing if pub re-clones the dep.

Not done: `upload_symbols: false` via ExportOptions — Xcode's Symbols/-in-IPA behavior is not verifiable without a real signed build here; the strip step is deterministic either way.

## Expected IPA delta (from CI numbers)

| Measure | Before (CI) | After | Δ |
|---|---|---|---|
| IPA uncompressed TOTAL | 253,948,172 | 149,337,184 | **−104,610,988 (−41.2%)** |
| IPA compressed (release asset) | 84,310,520 | **59,281,742 (measured on the repacked CI artifact)** | **−25,028,778 (−29.7%)** |
| TestFlight device size | ~157 MB | ~151 MB | −5.6 MB (the glb; Symbols never reached devices — ASC strips them) |

## Ratchet

`scripts/size_budget/fa-ios.tsv` (38 lines + TOTAL) seeded from the CI artifact with the diet applied — the exact post-cut floor. Wired into the build-ios leg: `python3 scripts/size_manifest.py check <ipa> --baseline scripts/size_budget/fa-ios.tsv` (+5% per-line and TOTAL budget, NEW-line guard) — same tool and semantics as the mac pass (#1227). The same step pins the owner hard constraint: the leg fails if `assets/wasm/{python,qjs,coreutils,lua}.wasm` or `LiteRtLm.framework` ever leave the IPA.

## Gate proofs (all local, against the CI artifact — no local iOS build)

- `size_manifest.py selftest` → **PASS**
- Failing-first: uncut CI IPA vs new floor → **exit 1**, `TOTAL +70.1%`, `Symbols/*` heavy lines flagged `NEW` — the ratchet demonstrably bites on the pre-diet shape
- Post-cut shape (repack of the CI IPA: `Symbols/` stripped, glb removed) vs floor → **exit 0**, `TOTAL -0.0%` (every entry byte-identical to the floor — symlink-preserving rezip changes no sizes)
- Keep-set assertions on the cut manifest: python/qjs/coreutils/lua wasm + LiteRtLm all present, `coach_anny` absent
- Workflow YAML re-parsed; build-ios step order: pub get → prune → build → strip → upload → ratchet+keep-set → FFI verify

## Honest disclosure

- No local iOS build exists in this PR: the fleet Mac cannot sign or build iOS, and per fleet policy local iOS AOT sizes are not evidence anyway. Every number above comes from CI run 37495702186's artifact + job log. The "post-cut" shape was produced by locally repacking **that CI artifact** with the exact commands the new strip step runs (plus the glb deletion the build-time prune does); the first CI-ios leg on this PR's merge train is the real end-to-end proof (device acceptance likewise CI/post-merge — js-apps wasm smoke is enforced statically by the keep-set gate here).
- Android legs, LiteRT, the WASM runtime, and the FFI-verify step are untouched.
- Fleet policy: this PR does not dispatch or rerun workflows; SM schedules CI."
  }
}

- name: Checkout repository from local mirror
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          MIRROR="$HOME/actions-runner-yoloit/mirror/flutter_agent_harness.git"
          cd /tmp
          rm -rf "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE"
          mkdir -p "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE"
          git clone --reference "$MIRROR" --depth=1 \
            https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness.git "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE"
          echo "Checked out: $(git -C $GITHUB_WORKSPACE log -1 --oneline)"

      # Persistent pinned SDK (issue #354): subosito/flutter-action with
      # cache: true on this PERSISTENT runner cost 5m39s setup (untar ~1GB
      # archive) + 8m47s POST (re-tar the whole SDK) per job — 14.5 of
      # 19.7 min around a 4-min build (run 34815041052). The composite
      # action keeps the SDK at ~/actions-runner-yoloit/flutter-sdk with a
      # .fah-version marker: subsecond reuse when the pin is unchanged,
      # exactly one download per pin bump, no cache POST step at all.
      # Still a pinned 3.47.x install — the runner's hardcoded
      # $HOME/.local/flutter is a stale 3.44.4, below the repo floor
      # >=3.47.0 (daily-publish #260).
      - name: Setup Flutter (self-hosted)
        uses: ./.github/actions/setup-flutter-selfhosted
        with:
          flutter-version: '3.47.x'

      - name: Setup environment (self-hosted)
        run: |
          echo "/opt/homebrew/opt/ruby/bin" >> $GITHUB_PATH
          echo "/opt/homebrew/bin" >> $GITHUB_PATH

      # gh-1275 AC3: fail fast before any build minute is spent — the full
      # gate rationale lives in .github/actions/assert-builtin-skills.
      - uses: ./.github/actions/assert-builtin-skills

      # gh-798 AC1/AC2: fail FAST before any build minute is spent when the
      # version about to be stamped is not above ASC's approved floor
      # (#785's class: altool 90062 at the END of the build). Reads the
      # SAME version source the build lane stamps (BUILD_NAME of the
      # version job); the lane skips named without ASC secrets (the upload
      # leg skips too) and fails closed if ASC is unreachable (E1, one
      # retry). The AC4 marker line lands in the leg log either way.
      - name: Assert TestFlight version floor
        working-directory: flutter_app
        env:
          BUILD_NAME: ${{ needs.version.outputs.version }}
          APP_STORE_CONNECT_KEY_ID: ${{ secrets.APP_STORE_CONNECT_KEY_ID }}
          APP_STORE_CONNECT_ISSUER_ID: ${{ secrets.APP_STORE_CONNECT_ISSUER_ID }}
          APP_STORE_CONNECT_KEY_CONTENT: ${{ secrets.APP_STORE_CONNECT_KEY_CONTENT }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          bundle install
          bundle exec fastlane ios assert_version_floor

      # Issue #726 (run 35491603044): pub has no retry for its git-dep
      # mirror clones — one flaky TCP connect to github.com:443 ("Failed
      # to connect ... after 11155 ms") failed the whole leg with no
      # retry. The bounded retry + deterministic-skew fail-fast now lives
      # in the shared composite action every enforce-lockfile pub get in
      # the repo rides (gh-1310; pinned by test/ci_pub_get_retry_guard_
      # test.dart).
      - name: Install Flutter dependencies
        uses: ./.github/actions/flutter-pub-get

      # #1331 size diet: js_widget_runtime declares `test/assets/` as a
      # package asset DIRECTORY, so its 5.6 MB coach_anny.glb test fixture
      # rides every app bundle. Nothing in the app references it (the #1227
      # mac pass verified by grep over flutter_app/lib, packages, lib and
      # the bundled JS apps — only the package's own tests load it, and
      # those live in the package repo). Removing the file is safe: the
      # pubspec declares the directory, not individual files.
      - name: Prune never-loaded package test fixture (#1331)
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          JS_WR=$(python3 -c '
            import json, pathlib
            cfg = json.loads(pathlib.Path("flutter_app/.dart_tool/package_config.json").read_text())
            print(next(p["rootUri"] for p in cfg["packages"] if p["name"] == "js_widget_runtime"))
          ')
          case "$JS_WR" in
            file://*) JS_WR=${JS_WR#file://} ;;
          esac
          case "$JS_WR" in
            /*) ;;
            *) JS_WR="$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/$JS_WR" ;;
          esac
          GLB="$JS_WR/test/assets/coach_anny.glb"
          if [ -f "$GLB" ]; then
            rm -f "$GLB"
            echo "pruned coach_anny.glb (5.6 MB never-loaded test fixture, #1331) from $JS_WR"
          else
            echo "coach_anny.glb already absent — nothing to prune"
          fi

      # The workspace is re-cloned every run, which wipes Pods/ and forces a
      # full pod install. Cache it keyed by the lockfile; $HOME-level caches
      # (pub-cache, CocoaPods download cache, Ruby gems, Flutter SDK) already
      # persist on the self-hosted runner.
      # v2: bust the cache — the Podfile.lock was stale (cupertino_http added
      # in 4bcac41 but the lockfile wasn't regenerated), so cached Pods were
      # missing the plugin's native code entirely. The build step's
      # `flutter build ios` runs `pod install` which regenerates the lockfile
      # with all registered plugins.
      - name: Cache CocoaPods (iOS)
        uses: actions/cache@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9 # v6.1.0
        with:
          path: flutter_app/ios/Pods
          key: ios-pods-v2-${{ hashFiles('flutter_app/ios/Podfile.lock') }}

      - name: Restore vendored WasmRun iOS framework
        timeout-minutes: 15
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          # The prebuilt XCFramework is excluded from git. Prefer the local
          # working copy on this self-hosted runner; fall back to the upstream
          # release asset if the local copy is unavailable.
          LOCAL_SRC="/Users/Uladzimir_Klyshevich/git/flutter_agent/vendor/wasm_run_flutter/ios/Frameworks/WasmRun.xcframework"
          DEST="vendor/wasm_run_flutter/ios/Frameworks"
          rm -rf "$DEST/WasmRun.xcframework"
          mkdir -p "$DEST"
          if [ -d "$LOCAL_SRC" ]; then
            echo "Using local framework: $LOCAL_SRC"
            cp -R "$LOCAL_SRC" "$DEST/"
          else
            echo "Local framework not found, downloading from upstream release..."
            # --retry alone skips transient mid-transfer resets (curl 56) —
            # the run-34709113737 failure: reset 3s into the 92.7 MB asset.
            curl -L --retry 3 --retry-all-errors --retry-delay 10 --max-time 600 \
              -o /tmp/WasmRun.xcframework.zip \
              https://github.com/juancastillo0/wasm_run/releases/download/wasm_run-v0.1.0/WasmRun.xcframework.zip
            unzip -q /tmp/WasmRun.xcframework.zip -d "$DEST"
          fi
          ls -la "$DEST/WasmRun.xcframework"

      - name: Validate iOS secrets
        env:
          IOS_P12_BASE64: ${{ secrets.IOS_P12_BASE64 }}
          IOS_P12_PASSWORD: ${{ secrets.IOS_P12_PASSWORD }}
          IOS_PROVISIONING_PROFILE_BASE64: ${{ secrets.IOS_PROVISIONING_PROFILE_BASE64 }}
        run: |
          if [ -z "$IOS_P12_BASE64" ]; then
            echo "::error::IOS_P12_BASE64 secret is not set"
            exit 1
          fi
          if [ -z "$IOS_P12_PASSWORD" ]; then
            echo "::error::IOS_P12_PASSWORD secret is not set"
            exit 1
          fi
          if [ -z "$IOS_PROVISIONING_PROFILE_BASE64" ]; then
            echo "::error::IOS_PROVISIONING_PROFILE_BASE64 secret is not set"
            exit 1
          fi
          echo "All required iOS secrets are present"

      - name: Import certificates and provisioning profile
        env:
          IOS_P12_BASE64: ${{ secrets.IOS_P12_BASE64 }}
          IOS_P12_PASSWORD: ${{ secrets.IOS_P12_PASSWORD }}
          IOS_PROVISIONING_PROFILE_BASE64: ${{ secrets.IOS_PROVISIONING_PROFILE_BASE64 }}
          IOS_LIVE_ACTIVITY_PROFILE_BASE64: ${{ secrets.IOS_LIVE_ACTIVITY_PROFILE_BASE64 }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          # Create a temporary keychain for this run (same pattern as learn.ai).
          security delete-keychain build.keychain 2>/dev/null || true
          secur…

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Per-artifact uncompressed size manifest + budget gate (#1096 AC1).

Emits the per-entry uncompressed size table (the issue's inventory format)
for a shipped artifact and fails the build when any tracked line regresses
beyond the budget (default +5%).

Usage:
  size_manifest.py emit   <artifact> [--min-bytes N]        # TSV to stdout
  size_manifest.py check  <artifact> --baseline FILE
                          [--budget-pct 5] [--init-if-missing]
                          [--manifest-out FILE]
  size_manifest.py selftest

`<artifact>` is a zip-family file (.zip/.ipa/.aab — uncompressed entry sizes
via zipfile) or a directory (tree of file sizes, for the web deploy root).

Manifest format (TSV; every row is `<bytes>\t<name>`, path-sorted. TOTAL
is an ordinary row — `<total_bytes>\tTOTAL` — and sorts among the paths;
do not rely on its position, the parser keys by name):
  <uncompressed_bytes>\t<path>
  <total_bytes>\tTOTAL

Gate semantics (`check`):
  - growth > budget%% on any baseline line or on TOTAL  -> FAIL
  - NEW line heavier than 5%% of the baseline TOTAL     -> FAIL
    (catches re-adding removed weight, e.g. a dropped interpreter coming
    back; canvaskit rev-dir churn on Flutter upgrades trips this too —
    that is by design: re-growth must be a conscious ack)
  - removed lines are improvements, reported only
  - --init-if-missing: no baseline file yet -> write it and pass with a
    loud notice (ratchet bootstrap; commit the file to arm the gate)
  - --reseed: overwrite an EXISTING baseline from this artifact and pass
    with a notice — the escape hatch for intentional growth; commit the
    rewritten file to make the new shape the floor

CI escape hatch for intentional growth: re-run locally with the same
artifact and `--reseed`, commit the rewritten baseline.
"""

import argparse
import sys
import zipfile
from pathlib import Path

# Per-line tracking floor: smaller files are noise (thousands of them
# jitter by whole percentages); the TOTAL line covers their aggregate.
MIN_BYTES = 64 * 1024
# A brand-new tracked line heavier than this share of the old TOTAL is
# re-growth, not rounding — fail it.
NEW_LINE_SHARE = 0.05


def iter_sizes(artifact: Path):
    """Yield (path, uncompressed_bytes) for every file in the artifact."""
    if artifact.is_file():
        # zip-family: .zip / .ipa / .aab / .apk
        with zipfile.ZipFile(artifact) as zf:
            for info in zf.infolist():
                if info.is_dir():
                    continue
                yield info.filename.replace("\t", " "), info.file_size
        return
    if artifact.is_dir():
        for p in sorted(artifact.rglob("*")):
            if p.is_file() and not p.is_symlink():
                yield p.relative_to(artifact).as_posix().replace("\t", " "), p.stat().st_size
        return
    raise SystemExit(f"size_manifest: artifact not found: {artifact}")


def build_manifest(artifact: Path, min_bytes: int) -> "dict[str, int]":
    sizes = dict(iter_sizes(artifact))
    manifest = {p: n for p, n in sizes.items() if n >= min_bytes}
    manifest["TOTAL"] = sum(sizes.values())
    return manifest


def fmt_table(manifest: "dict[str, int]") -> str:
    width = max((len(p) for p in manifest), default=5)
    lines = [f"{manifest[p]:>12}  {p.ljust(width)}" for p in sorted(manifest) if p != "TOTAL"]
    lines.append("-" * (width + 14))
    lines.append(f"{manifest['TOTAL']:>12}  TOTAL")
    return "\n".join(lines)


def load_baseline(path: Path) -> "dict[str, int]":
    baseline = {}
    for line in path.read_text().splitlines():
        if not line.strip():
            continue
        size, _, name = line.partition("\t")
        baseline[name] = int(size)
    if "TOTAL" not in baseline:
        raise SystemExit(f"size_manifest: baseline {path} has no TOTAL line")
    return baseline


def write_baseline(path: Path, manifest: "dict[str, int]") -> None:
    path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    lines = [f"{manifest[p]}\t{p}" for p in sorted(manifest)]
    path.write_text("\n".join(lines) + "\n")


def check(artifact: Path, baseline_path: Path, budget_pct: float,
          init_if_missing: bool = False, reseed: bool = False,
          manifest_out=None) -> int:
    manifest = build_manifest(artifact, MIN_BYTES)
    if manifest_out:
        write_baseline(manifest_out, manifest)

    if not baseline_path.exists():
        if init_if_missing:
            write_baseline(baseline_path, manifest)
            print(f"::notice::size_manifest: baseline initialized from this "
                  f"artifact — COMMIT {baseline_path} to arm the gate")
            print(fmt_table(manifest))
            return 0
        print(f"::error::size_manifest: baseline {baseline_path} missing "
              f"(run with --init-if-missing to seed it)")
        return 2

    if reseed:
        write_baseline(baseline_path, manifest)
        print(f"::notice::size_manifest: baseline RESEEDED from this "
              f"artifact — {baseline_path} rewritten; COMMIT it to make "
              f"the new shape the floor")
        print(fmt_table(manifest))
        return 0

    baseline = load_baseline(baseline_path)
    base_total = baseline["TOTAL"]
    failures = []
    grew, shrank, new, removed = [], [], [], []

    for name in sorted(set(baseline) | set(manifest)):
        if name == "TOTAL":
            continue
        old, cur = baseline.get(name), manifest.get(name)
        if old is None and cur is not None:
            new.append((name, cur))
        elif cur is None:
            removed.append((name, old))
        elif cur > old:
            grew.append((name, old, cur))
        elif cur < old:
            shrank.append((name, old, cur))

    for name, old, cur in grew:
        pct = (cur - old) / old * 100 if old else float("inf")
        if pct > budget_pct:
            failures.append(f"  GREW    +{pct:6.1f}%  {name}  {old} -> {cur}")
    total_pct = (manifest["TOTAL"] - base_total) / base_total * 100 if base_total else 0.0
    if total_pct > budget_pct:
        failures.append(f"  TOTAL   +{total_pct:6.1f}%  {base_total} -> {manifest['TOTAL']}")
    for name, cur in new:
        if cur > NEW_LINE_SHARE * base_total:
            failures.append(f"  NEW     {'':>8}  {name}  {cur} bytes "
                            f"(> {NEW_LINE_SHARE:.0%} of baseline TOTAL)")

          f"baseline: {baseline_path})")
    print(fmt_table(manifest))
    if shrank:
        print(f"improvements: {len(shrank)} line(s) shrank, "
              f"{len(removed)} line(s) removed")
        for name, old, cur in shrank[:10]:
            print(f"  shrank  {name}  {old} -> {cur}")
        for name, old in removed[:10]:
            print(f"  removed {name}  ({old} bytes)")
    if failures:
        print(f"::error::size budget regression in {artifact} "
              f"({len(failures)} line(s) beyond +{budget_pct}%):")
        for f in failures:
            print(f)
        print("intentional growth? re-seed the floor with: python3 "
              "scripts/size_manifest.py check <artifact> --baseline "
              f"{baseline_path} --reseed")
        return 1
    print(f"size budget OK (TOTAL {total_pct:+.1f}% vs baseline)")
    return 0

All required context — ticket description, PR diff, CI status, and related materials — has already been prepared in the `input/` folder. Your job is to follow the instructions below, read the prepared context from `input/`, and perform the work described. Do not ask for identifiers; the context is already available locally. ```mermaid flowchart TD G1["⚠️ Review Guidelines — evaluate against existing codebase patterns"] G2["Before reviewing, explore the project's code structure, architecture, and testing patterns"] G3["If AGENTS.md exists → READ it — defines coding styles to check against"] G4["Flag deviations from established patterns unless justified in PR description"] G1 --> G2 --> G3 --> G4 ``` # PR Review General Guidelines ## Review flow ```mermaid flowchart TD START([PR ready for review]) --> READ["1. Read input context:
instruction.md, ticket.md, pr_info.md,
pr_diff.txt, pr_files.txt, ci_failures.md,

pr_discussions_raw.json"] READ --> DIFF["2. Run diff checklist on pr_diff.txt"] DIFF --> FILES["3. Read full content of every changed file"] FILES --> CODEGRAPH["4. Use CodeGraph:
callers/callees of changed symbols,
search for sensitive patterns,
impact analysis"] CODEGRAPH --> DIMS["5. Evaluate review dimensions:
Security · Architecture/OOP · Code quality
Test coverage · Duplication · Backward compatibility"] DIMS --> SEVERITY["6. Classify each finding:
BLOCKING / IMPORTANT / SUGGESTION"] SEVERITY --> EXHAUST["7. Exhaustive pass:
re-read changed files,
surface ALL remaining issues"] EXHAUST --> OUTPUT["8. Write outputs:
pr_review.json · pr_review_general.md · pr_review_comments/*.md"] OUTPUT --> END([End]) ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Impact analysis (CodeGraph or grep fallback) Use CodeGraph to find "what could break": - `codegraph_callers` / `codegraph_callees` on modified public symbols - `codegraph_search` for: `PAT_TOKEN`, `secrets.`, `github.token`, `previousViewModel` - `codegraph_impact` before flagging architectural changes **If CodeGraph unavailable**, use grep and document it: ```bash grep -rn "changedFunctionName" --include="*.ts" . grep -rn "secrets\.\|github\.token" . ``` ## 5. Review dimensions Rate the PR across all relevant dimensions: | Dimension | What to check | |---|---| | **Security** | injection, unsafe interpolation, secret leakage, missing permissions, unsafe defaults | | **Architecture / OOP** | SRP, coupling, abstraction consistency, provider/repository boundaries | | **Code quality** | naming, complexity, error handling, logging, comments | | **Tests** | coverage for new/changed paths, meaningful assertions, no brittle string-only tests | | **Duplication** | copy-paste, duplicated logic across files, duplicated configuration | | **Backward compatibility** | public API changes, migration paths, default behavior | | **Performance** | unnecessary rebuilds, heavy sync operations, missing timeouts | | **Workflow / CI safety** | (when `.github/workflows/` changes) secret declarations, ref pinning, permissions, timeouts | ## 6. Severity classification Classify every finding before writing outputs: - **BLOCKING** — merge would cause a bug, security issue, data loss, or CI break. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. Outputs Write the standard review artifacts: - `outputs/pr_review.json` — structured data with `recommendation`, `summary`, `inlineComments`, `issueCounts` - `outputs/pr_review_general.md` — 1-2 paragraph general PR comment - `outputs/pr_review_comments/*.md` — one file per detailed inline comment **Inline comment lines must be present in the PR diff.** GitHub review threads can only be attached to added or context lines inside a diff hunk. If `pr_diff.txt` is truncated, run `git diff origin/{baseBranch}...HEAD` to locate the correct line numbers. Findings on unchanged code outside the diff belong in `outputs/pr_review_general.md`, not as inline comments. Do NOT write `outputs/response.md`; the review is posted to GitHub only. ```mermaid flowchart TD O1["Write outputs/pr_review.json — structured data for GitHub PR review…
